text: Ten N=64, e<=0.5 seeds now have 5-step trajectories (56-58, 62, 63, 65-69), with persistent 0.1-bar formation spread over steps 65-100. Is the 0.1-bar step driven mostly by how long a run dwells just below the threshold (for example seed 62 at 0.095-0.097 for steps 80-95)? Would a smoothed crossing, such as fitting a logistic curve to the margin trajectory and taking its midpoint, cut the seed-to-seed spread compared with both the persistent and the half-final measures?
